title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theater on 1969-02-07
lineage: SBD > MC > DAT > HHb > CDR > EAC (secure) > CD Wave > Cool Edit Pro > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1969 late‑show captured on a slightly compressed cassette soundboard; stellar performances of The Other One, Alligator and Death Don't make it a must‑hear despite hiss and fade‑ins.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers an explosive late‑show from early ’69 with Jerry Garcia in top form – acid‑drenched leads, pyrotechnic solos and a raging The Other One that drives the set.  Alligator, Cryptical Envelopment, Death Don't, Caution Jam and the infamous Feedback sequence are highlighted as peak moments, while Phil’s counter‑theme bass work adds depth.  Technically the tape suffers from cassette hiss, heavy compression and occasional fade‑ins/out, but the mix remains listenable and the performance more than compensates for those flaws.

ai_rating.rationale: Over ten detailed reviews uniformly praise the musical performance (standout jams, high energy) and acknowledge only moderate recording issues; the strong show weight drives a rating near the top of the scale.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Cassette master with noticeable hiss, heavy compression making EQ difficult, and fade‑ins/out; mix is decent overall and all instruments/vocals remain audible.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Late‑show set is described as relentless and high‑energy, with extended jams that flow naturally from Alligator into drums, jam, Primal Alligator, Caution and Feedback; the second half consistently outshines the first.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is repeatedly called acid‑drenched, pyrotechnic, pure blues emotion and a nonstop high‑energy force throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil Lesh provides a counter‑theme to Jerry’s leads, delivers a notable bass solo and adds depth to the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: One reviewer felt Bob Weir's playing was not particularly strong this night.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers are praised for fast, furious playing and for creating powerful jam sections that drive tracks like Caution Jam and Feedback.
